cues.mood: airy dawn haze → bright, driving build → confident groove → plum half-time rewind with a four-beat hole in time → a two-chord verdict at the hinge → the brightest lift, a warm D-major resolve and one soft final button
cues.key: D major with a lydian lift (E/D); B minor (relative) for the time-travel chapter; resolves to D6/9
cues.instrumentation: TR-909 kick (tuned down; in the loop, drive and lift layered over a sine kick with a fast pitch drop), closed and open hat, clap, snare/toms (one fill), crash (two, hpf) and rim (soft, filtered); dry 909 rim clacks; sine sub (D1-A1, lpf 120); round sine bass (off-beat 8ths, lpf 200); warm pad of two saws detuned ±7 cents (lpf 600-1400, slow filter envelopes); plucks are filter-envelope saws with a dotted-8th delay (not triangles: nothing bell-like); a square stuck pluck (F#4); felt piano (piano, lpf 1300-2000); a high 16th pluck arpeggio (hpf 2500) in the lift; pink-noise risers, a white-noise air layer above 7.5 kHz, reversed saw swells; tape-stop by pitch envelope (-24 st). No bells, celesta, glockenspiel, music box or vibraphone.
cues.notes:
CURRENT CLOCK (timeline 82.708 s, locked; re-fitted 2026-10-14 by the music director after round-1 review, revised by the composer after critic round 1; this paragraph is the only time authority). Window 0.000-82.708 (82.708 s = the whole film; body 41.354 cycles at setcps(.5), tail 6 s). Shots (start s): ch01-s01 0.000, ch01-s03 4.583, ch02-s01 7.500, ch02-s02 10.417, ch03-s01 13.917, ch04-s01 20.708, ch04-s02 25.542, ch04-s03 28.958, ch05-s01 36.375, ch05-s02 39.167, ch05-s03 50.500, ch05-s04 58.333, ch06-s01 67.083, ch06-s02 73.917 (14 shots; ch05-s05 was cut). THE WHOLE FILM, one arranged track (intro, body, outro): bright, warm product-promo electronica in D major with a lydian lift (E/D), B minor for the time-travel chapter, nominally 122 BPM on a tempo map that puts every cut on a bar line (one push lands a 16th early: the ch05-s02 cut; the ch04-s02 cut is a bar line on the regenerated map). Motifs: M1 'Point it' (plucked hook D5 E5 F#5 A5, answer B5 A5), M2 'Always on' (soft 909 four-on-the-floor, 16th hats, clap on 2 and 4, the dry rim/woodblock clack), M3 'Haze' (warm saw pad, the sentence Dmaj9 E/D Bm9 Gmaj9, sine sub), M4 'In time' (tape-stop, reversed swell, frame clacks, four beats of silence, the stuck one-note pluck), M5 'The verdict' (felt piano Asus2 then D). Machines clack or tick, never chime: no celesta, glockenspiel, music box, vibes or bells.

HAZE AND LIFT (ch01, intensity 0.2-0.3, no drums): the haze pad at full haze level from the first frame (a sine-sub swell and white-noise air under it), M1's first note on the downbeat where 'Imagine' starts; pads alone with the filter opening on 'sweep'; a filtered 16th arpeggio in M1's notes; a noise riser and pad swell crest on the blur cut and land on the 'Introducing' downbeat as a muted thump, the pad stepping to E/D; a tight filtered clack per frame stamp from 'stamps'; a sine sub drop on 'mark' ("Replay QA"); the arpeggio accelerates with the map and a reversed whoosh fills the whip's beat.

BUILD (ch02, 0.45, about -22 LUFS S): a soft, round kick enters on 'caret' (909 at low velocity behind lpf 1000), no bass; typed keys as tiny muted clicks under 'keys' to 'typed'; under "Point it at your app" only those ticks and one soft A5 on 'app', so the hook's first clear statement is the full-voice one in the breath after 'typed'; quiet hats enter on the ch02-s02 cut; a small filtered stab and brace transient on 'url' ("Just a quick chat").

LOOP (ch03, 0.55-0.65, about -20.5 S): clap on 2 and 4, the kick opens (lpf 1800) and the hats step up; one dry clack per check on 'b-check1', 'b-check2' and 'b-check3' (the shot's only accents); a one-bar snare/tom fill with a noise riser lands on the ch04 cut.

DRIVE (ch04, 0.75, about -19 S): full groove, bright 16th hats with a light open hat on 2 and 4, a round sine bass, M1 in thirds, the sentence one chord per bar. The triplet of proofs: a filtered stab on each proof's cut (the ch04-s01, ch04-s02 and ch04-s03 cuts); a muted pluck on 'b-hosted', a brace-snap transient on 'b-schedule', soft ticks on the date strip from 'b-strip'; three rising plucked accents on 'b-staging', 'b-preview', 'b-local'; the brace snap on 'b-pr', a soft off-beat clack per chip from 'b-chips', a muted tick on 'b-check'. On 'b-tapestop' everything pitch-falls (tape-stop) into the ch05 cut.

REWIND (ch05, 0.4-0.5, B minor, half time): a muffled kick; a reversed Bm9 swell that crests and cuts off on 'intime' (the word "time"); a dry frame tick per beat from 'rewind' for two bars as the playhead runs back, each softer and duller than the last; a soft frame clack per beat from 'ribbon'; on 'Four' ("Four dropped frames") EVERY lane stops dead for exactly four beats with no reverb tail (the dropped frames heard as missing time); the kick returns on 'click'. A dry, unpitched clatter on 'shatter'; pads low (Em9 behind lpf 700) with a half-time pulse under them (muffled kick on 1, filtered rim on 3, low velocity) and a very quiet high tick per beat above the voice band, under "Twenty-five of twenty-seven" and "A screen recording can't see that"; kick and a warm B1 bass return on 'matchcut' and the harmony lifts G to D on 'rootcause' (the last "can"). From 'counter' a 16th closed-hat pulse that STOPS DEAD on 'u258'; under it M1 frozen on F#4 (one note, one length: the stuck checkpoint); three muted plucks from 'snapback' settle on 'place'; the pluck restarts once on 'over' ("starting over").

VERDICT, NOW AT THE HINGE (the unnarrated verdict shot was cut; intensity 0.35 to 0.6): the verdict lives in the breath after "starting over" (from the end of L0508 to the ch06-s01 cut). A soft rim tick and a quiet A1 sub carry from 'over'; felt piano at full voice: a short, open Asus2 as L0508 ends, over pads thinned to open fifths (A-E-B, no third); then the ramp in the same breath: the pad's filter opens, a short pink-noise riser and a 32nd snare roll on the last beat; the warmer, fuller D (D-A-E fifths, the piano doubling it) lands on the ch06-s01 downbeat with the lift (a lift, not a cliff).

LIFT AND END CARD (ch06, 0.85 then resolve, the loudest section at about -17.5 S, its extra level from the top): full band, the brightest hats, a white-noise air sheen above 7 kHz and a high 16th pluck arpeggio over the brightest voicing. Under all of L0601 and L0602 the top stays out of his consonant band (2-5 kHz): the arpeggio high-passed at 6 kHz and soft (its breaths are too short to bloom into, so it is not gated phrase by phrase), the closed hats eased 3 dB at hpf 8500, the open hat only on 2 and 4 (velocity .25 or lower, hpf 9000, release .05), the claps at velocity .4 behind lpf 2500; the lift keeps its weight in the sub, kick and pad. THE BLOOM is the one swell, in the breath from the end of 'confirm' to 'Replay': the arpeggio full (hpf 2500, +2 dB), the air sheen at full level, open hats on every 8th to the end-card cut, the claps full, and M1 in octaves landing its A a 16th ahead of the end-card cut; the lydian E/D; a low thump (a stab with no filter envelope, lpf 1200) under each woven word on 'w1', 'w2', 'w3', 'w4', 'w5'; a clack on 'chip'; a short riser into the end card; Dmaj9 on its cut, E/D on 'tag1' with M1's answer B4 under it, A13sus on 'grow' with the answer's A4: the end card states the answer, soft and dark; on 'managed' the full band strikes D6/9 once (kick, sub D1, wide pad) and the pluck plays M1's call D5 E5 F#5 A5 as a fast upward roll in 32nds (about 60 ms apart, each note held into the chord, velocity .7 rising to .8, lpf 900, lpenv 2): the hook arriving home; the drums stop there. The pad (D6/9 voiced d3 a3 e4 f#4 b4 over sub D1) rings under "Catch bugs that only exist in time" and releases, with the sub, a 16th or two before the button. Then ONE final button on the first 16th after 'time' ends, struck into air: sub D1, a muted filtered-saw pluck D5/F#5 (lpf 600), one dry 909 rim clack (velocity .45); no bells or chimes; with the qa.replay.io caret settle: that is the last strike. Nothing is struck after it; it rings (sub release 2.8 s, the pluck's room and delay) for more than 2.3 s before the fade begins. Target 10-11 dB line-over-music on L0601 and L0602.

UNDER THE VOICE (male mid-life baritone): keep 250 Hz-3.5 kHz sparse while he speaks (pads voiced from D3 up with hpf 180, lpf 800-1200, low velocity; the roots in the sine sub below 110 Hz; a sine bass under lpf 200; in the loop, drive and lift a hybrid kick, a sine kick under a quieter 909, keeps 110-250 Hz clear of his fundamental); brightness lives above 5 kHz (hats, air, pluck transients); plucks and stabs speak fully in the gaps and on the hits. Aim the render near -20 LUFS I, TP -3 dBTP or lower, zero clipped samples, zero Strudel errors.

COMPOSER REALISATION (m01.strudel, re-fitted to the 82.71 s clock after ch05-s05 was cut): the tempo map BARS was regenerated from the clock, not nudged (score/motifs.md §1 has the new map and hit grid); every cut is a bar line except the ch05-s02 push, so proof two's stab lands on the ch04-s02 downbeat and its brace snap on 'Against'. M1 is stated where the voice is not: a single soft A5 on 'app', then complete at full voice in the breath after 'typed' (its first clear statement), in thirds in the breath before 'Against' and as the pickup into proof three, softly with the G# on the E/D bar under 'b-chips', in octaves in the bloom after 'confirm', landing its A a 16th ahead of the end-card cut, its answer B4-A4 under the tagline, and its call rolled into the D6/9 on 'managed'. In the haze M1 is revealed one note per bar as the arpeggio's top voice; the haze pad reaches full level within its quarter-second attack (no fade-in). The tape-stop is a one-beat bar from 'b-tapestop' to the ch05 cut: the G chord and a G1 saw fall two octaves over a slowed kick. The rewind pads are reversed saw swells cresting on each bar line from the ch05 cut; the last one is dry and is sucked into the hole on 'Four', which lasts exactly four beats at the rewind tempo and ends on the kick under the word 'click' (the hole measures about -80 dBFS RMS). Under L0505 and L0506 the hush keeps the pull-back with a half-time pulse: a muffled 909 kick (lpf 360) on 1 and a filtered rim (lpf 1300) on 3, both at low velocity, under the quiet high tick. The verdict is the 2/4 hinge bar after 'over': the felt-piano Asus2 (A3 E4 B4) a 16th into it over pads thinned to A-E-B, a rim tick, a quiet A1 sub, the pad filter opening, a pink riser and a 32nd snare roll on its last beat; the piano's D (D3 A3 E4 F#4) lands with the band on the ch06-s01 downbeat. The agent pair inside ch06-s01 gets no musical moment of its own. In the lift the top is kept out of 2-5 kHz under all of L0601 and L0602 (arpeggio hpf 6000 and soft, closed hats -3 dB at hpf 8500, open hat on 2 and 4 only at .22 behind hpf 9000, claps .4 behind lpf 2500, woven-word stabs as low thumps with lpenv 0 and lpf 1200), and the sub, the sine kick and the bass carry about 2 dB more weight than in the drive so the section's level holds; the bloom from the end of 'confirm' to 'Replay' opens everything (arpeggio hpf 2500 +2 dB, air full, open hats on every 8th, M1 in octaves). Measured in the 2-5 kHz band, the music under L0601 and L0602 sits about 4.7-4.9 dB below the music under the drive lines, and the bloom rises about 8 dB above the music under L0601. On 'managed' the band strikes D6/9 under M1's rolled call (the pad filter settles dark under the last line) and the drums stop. The pad and the sub release a 16th or two before the button, which falls on the first 16th after 'time' into air: sub D1, the D5/F#5 pluck muted (lpf 600), one dry 909 rim clack at .45; it is the last strike (the analysis finds it within one 20 ms frame), and the sub (release 2.8 s) and the pluck's room and delay ring out into the fade.
